Investing.com -- Bank of America has highlighted Micron Technology as its top stock pick, maintaining a buy rating with a price objective of $1,550, significantly above the current trading price of $877.55.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The firm's confidence stems from recent investor meetings with Micron's senior leadership team in New York and Boston, where management outlined the company's strategic positioning in the memory market.

Following the company's technology and product webinar, Bank of America analysts met with Micron's Chief Operating Officer Manish Bhatia, Chief Technology Officer Scott DeBoer, Chief Financial Officer Mark Murphy, and Corporate Vice President of Investor Relations Satya Kumar. The meetings reinforced the firm's positive outlook on memory's long-term value, with management indicating tighter market conditions expected in calendar years 2027 and 2028 compared to 2026.

Bank of America rates Micron as a buy with a $1,550 price target. The firm emphasizes five key factors supporting its recommendation. First, memory remains the critical enabler of artificial intelligence performance and power efficiency.

Second, current memory de-specifications reflect supply shortages rather than reduced significance, with more memory capacity translating to higher token output per dollar.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Third, supply chain agreements provide greater flexibility spanning three to five years as take-or-pay arrangements with financial commitments.

Fourth, Micron maintains technology leadership across high-bandwidth memory, DRAM, and NAND products.

Fifth, the company plans to increase capital returns to shareholders beginning December 9.

Management views memory as increasingly becoming the most critical architectural component in AI systems. Current supply chain agreements cover approximately 35 percent of total sales, with a target of 50 percent by calendar year 2030. The pricing framework includes a floor well above prior cycle highs.

Micron's product roadmap includes support for HBM configurations from 4-hi through 16-hi, four additional planar DRAM nodes after 1-gamma, and G11 NAND targeting over 400 layers by late 2027. The company expects to generate approximately $150-200 billion in annual free cash flow during calendar years 2027-2028, with approximately $35 billion currently authorized for share repurchases.

title: HubSpot faces narrower growth beat and possible guidance cut, BofA says
detail:
HubSpot faces narrower growth beat and possible guidance cut, BofA says
Proactive

HUBS
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
HubSpot faces narrower growth beat and possible guidance cut, BofA says Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

HubSpot (NYSE:HUBS), the customer relationship management platform, is likely to deliver a smaller-than-usual beat against its third-quarter constant currency growth guidance, Bank of America (BofA) said, maintaining its 'underperform' rating.

HubSpot is due to report third-quarter results on November 4 after market close.

The analyst's checks suggest the buying environment is unlikely to improve soon, with channel partners reporting mixed feedback that was modestly more negative than in the second quarter.

BofA expects constant currency growth, which strips out exchange rate effects, to beat guidance by only 1.4 percentage points, against a typical beat of more than 2 points.

A 7% workforce reduction in October came alongside a reiteration of its third-quarter and full-year guidance, making an outright cut less likely.

HubSpot's shares have risen about 23% over the past month, and BofA said investors are looking for signs of demand stabilisation and early evidence of an AI-driven revenue opportunity.

HubSpot cut its 2026 net revenue retention outlook last quarter to roughly flat year on year, from expected growth of 1 to 2 percentage points, implying net revenue retention of about 103.5%.

BofA says net revenue retention needs to reach at least 103% in the third quarter, up 1 percentage point quarter on quarter, to avoid another reduction in guidance.

HubSpot began rolling out a simplified "platform plus credits" pricing model to new customers in Europe, the Middle East and Africa at the start of the fourth quarter, with a wider rollout to Asia-Pacific and US customers possible within three to six months.

Channel feedback suggests initial contract values could be 10% to 30% lower under the new model, creating near-term billings risk despite potential annual contract value growth as credit usage scales.

The bank said healthy win rates against competitors such as Salesforce could support the shares if customer buying patterns or budgets show signs of improvement.

title: Freight Costs Force Bank of America to Cut Target Price on Off-Price
detail:
Freight Costs Force Bank of America to Cut Target Price on Off-Price
Sourcing Journal · Getty Images
Arthur Zaczkiewicz
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:41 PM EDT 4 min read
BAC
ROST
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Analysts at Bank of America are reducing their stock price objectives (PO) on the off-price retailers they track—TJX Cos., Ross Stores and Burlington.

Analysts Lorraine Hutchinson and Mary Sport said in a research note that they were cutting back their PO estimates by 3 for TJX Cos. and Ross Stores and 6 percent for Burlington "to reflect higher freight costs" beginning in Q2 2027 when contracts renew. They said that April 2027 rates will ultimately determine the headwind, but they modeled a 15 percent increase for domestic freight and an 80 percent increase in ocean freight.

Still, the analysts said they expect the oﬀ-price sector to outperform in an inflationary environment "that constrains purchasing power." As a result, the analysts are retaining their "Buy" ratings on TJX Cos., Ross Stores and Burlington.

"Higher prices for necessities, combined with persistently elevated fuel prices, leaves consumers with less to spend on discretionary goods and should reinforce value-seeking behavior," they said. "We think oﬀ-price is well positioned to capitalize on that."

In formulating their analysis, Hutchinson and Sport looked at historical data to help inform their view. They also sought out their colleagues at the firm. "Rather than wait for April, we worked with our Global Transport team to assess where rates could settle and have incorporated 60 [basis points] of incremental freight pressure starting in 2Q," the analysts said.

The analysts said while the 15/80 increase model is challenging, "this remains more benign than 2022, when higher rates pressured margins by 200 to 300 [basis points]," they said. "Our domestic assumption reflects current rates relative to April 2026, while our ocean assumption incorporates normalization from today's 168 percent aﬅer peak season."

Then there are the other sectors to consider, such as department and specialty stores. Looking back to 2021, specialty retailers absorbed an even greater freight impact than off-price, although much of that pressure reflected retailers shifting to air freight to avoid severe port congestion and ensure product reached shelves for holiday," the analysts said. "We do see some risk to specialty retail if these higher rates persist, but off-price sellers sell products at lower prices, so shipping can be a heavier burden."

Fortinet's (FTNT) Q3 results indicate a slowdown in some key metrics that suggest that Q2 was abnormally strong and may reflect some demand pull-forward, BofA Securities said in a note Thursday.

The investment firm said that these dynamics combined with "lingering component and inventory issues,
now offset positive macro tailwinds due to AI."

BofA said the company's Q3 results were a mixed print that "fell well short" of investor expectations for some key metrics. The investment firm noted revenue grew 20.5% to $2.078 billion and beat consensus estimate for $2.066 billion, and EPS of $0.94 also beat the Street's estimate of $0.86.

However, key metrics were missed, BofA said, adding the company's 3Q Product revenue rose 37%, which is a slowdown from Q2's 52% growth and below the expectations of investors that BofA spoke with.

Also, Services revenue, which BofA said should be "more durable and predictable" missed the consensus estimate, the note said.

BofA downgraded Fortinet to neutral from buy and lowered the company's price target to $140 from $220.

Fortinet shares were falling over 22% in recent trading.

title: Can BAC's Branch Expansion & AI Push Drive Long-Term Growth?
detail:
Can BAC's Branch Expansion & AI Push Drive Long-Term Growth?

WFC
JPM

Trading disclosure

Bank of America BAC is stepping up its branch expansion efforts, with its recent entry into Wisconsin and planned openings in Alabama and Louisiana reinforcing its growth strategy. The bank intends to add 19 financial centers in Wisconsin by 2030, alongside 18 locations across Alabama and Greater New Orleans beginning in 2027.

With approximately 3,500 financial centers reaching nearly 83% of the U.S. population, BAC plans to add 50 locations annually. Its growing physical presence should complement its established digital platform, enabling the bank to attract customers in newer markets while deepening relationships through personalized financial advice. This could boost demand for mortgages, wealth management and business banking services, supporting diversified revenue growth.

Meanwhile, BAC's focus on modernizing its existing network should enhance service quality and strengthen its competitive position. Since 2016, the bank has invested more than $5 billion in opening and upgrading financial centers. It has completed more than 400 renovations this year, with more than 300 additional projects planned. These upgrades should improve customer experience and employee productivity, potentially supporting stronger returns from its physical infrastructure over time.

BAC's AI initiatives further reinforce its long-term growth potential. While more than 95% of client interactions occur digitally, approximately 10 million specialist appointments over the past year highlight sustained demand for in-person expertise. AI-powered tools like Plan My Day and EricaAssist are helping employees deliver more efficient and personalized services. Notably, management expects benefits from its AI project pipeline to rise from $250-$300 million in 2026 to $700 million in 2027, indicating meaningful scope for productivity gains and cost savings.

BAC's integrated approach to physical expansion and digital innovation should support sustainable revenue growth and improved operating leverage. A wider distribution network, coupled with AI-led efficiencies, could strengthen profitability and long-term earnings prospects. However, elevated investment spending, intense competition and the time required for new branches to achieve profitability remain concerning. Nevertheless, these initiatives position BAC favorably to capitalize on evolving customer preferences and drive long-term growth.

BAC's Competitive Landscape

JPMorgan JPM is also expanding its branch network while investing in digital capabilities to deepen customer relationships and capture market share. JPMorgan's strategy of combining physical accessibility with technological innovation should support deposit gathering, lending activity and wealth management opportunities. Like BAC, JPMorgan is positioned to benefit from stronger customer engagement and diversified revenue streams.

Likewise, Wells Fargo WFC is focusing on digital transformation and operational efficiency to strengthen its consumer banking franchise. Wells Fargo's investments in technology and customer service improvements should support retention and cross-selling opportunities. Similar to BAC, Wells Fargo aims to balance personalized banking services with digital convenience, although cost pressures and competition could limit near-term benefits.

title: The 5 Numbers That Matter Most in a Bank's Earnings Report
detail:
The 5 Numbers That Matter Most in a Bank's Earnings Report
James Brumley, The Motley Fool

WFC

NVDA

Most major banks, including JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), and Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC), have already reported their third-quarter earnings. And all in all, they weren't great.

JPMorgan's numbers came up short, as did BofA's. Although Wells Fargo's earnings topped estimates, revenue of just under $21.9 billion missed the analyst consensus of $22.3 billion. These stocks' performances have been mixed in the meantime.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

And this raises the question: What really drives the response to banks' earnings? These five metrics arguably mean the most.

1. Net interest income: When it comes right down to it, banks' core business is charging interest on loaned money they borrowed themselves. The difference between a bank's internal cost of borrowed capital and the interest it's collecting from its loan customers is net interest income, or NII. For perspective, a little over half of Bank of America's Q3 income was interest income.

2. Provision for credit losses: Although in some ways it seems like they shouldn't know, the fact is, most banks have a pretty good idea from one quarter to the next of how much of their loan portfolio is about to be written off as a loss.

3. Common equity tier 1: Common equity tier 1 isn't a measure that means much most of the time. When it does matter, though, it matters in a big way. Simply put, it's the amount of high-quality capital a bank can use to offset shock losses and continue to function.

4. Return on tangible common equity: A bank's return on tangible common equity -- or ROTCE -- wasn't always a concern, nor was it always calculated and/or disclosed. It only became prominent in the early 2000s, in response to unexpected but predictable trouble. Just as the name suggests, it's a measure of how much return shareholders are getting on their collective investment.

5. Earnings per share: Finally, while banks clearly have several industry-specific metrics to weigh, they're still businesses ultimately meant to generate profits. Per-share earnings remain an important, all-encompassing figure.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.
